newsitem.title: USA: Toro says FY96 sales better than planned.
newsitem.headline: Toro says FY96 sales better than planned.

text.p: Toro Co said Wednesday its sales for fiscal 1996 of $930.9 million, up from $919.4 million a year ago, were better than expected.

"We planned for a sluggish economy and our sales results were better than expected," Kendrick Melrose, chairman, said in a statement. "Because we had planned for a modest year we monitored retail demand very closely and this, coupled with our added flexibility and responsiveness in production and shipping, enabled us to manage our overall inventories going into the 1997 season."
Toro shares were up one at 34-7/8 at midday.

Melrose said that Toro's primary markets, the residential and the professional turf maintenance markets, did well in fiscal 1996 despite a late spring and an increasingly competitive marketplace. Strong performances in several of the company's diverse product lines offset slower growth in others.

Earlier, Toro, which makes lawn care and other outdoor maintenance products, reported earnings for the fourth quarter ended October 31 of $0.37 a share, up from $0.32 a year ago. For fiscal 1996, it earned $2.90 a share, up from $2.50.
The residential market was led by good snowthrower sales that resulted from heavy snows, particularly on the East Coast.
Revenues for Toro's professional turf markets grew to half of Toro sales in 1996, helping to diversify the company's performance in the non-consumer sector in the United States and around the world.

Sales of domestic irrigation systems increased, as did sales of international commercial equipment. Sales of domestic commercial equipment grew more slowly than in past years due to increased competition, Toro added.

International sales increased 16.5 percent for the year and 30.2 percent for the fourth quarter over comparable periods a year ago, led by sales of commercial equipment to golf courses in core and emerging markets around the world.

"The long term outlook for our business is healthy and we are optimistic about the new fiscal year," Melrose said. "We are confident we can continue to manage our business for improved levels of profitability, despite a conservative outlook for sales growth."
